subject: Private deployment — network probe & SLO next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@maplepay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment — network probe & SLO next steps

Thanks for the call today — good alignment on the high-level routing and the customer use case. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can get a targeted performance validation window on your VPC/private deployment.

Summary of requirements (as we heard them):
- Streaming/real-time inference use case: tail latency is the priority for UI calls (short prompts, interactive).
- Target SLOs provided by MaplePay: p99 streaming/response <= 120ms, p50 <= 35ms.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~600 requests/sec during peak (burst to 1k for <10m).
- Concurrent sessions (hot KV caching required): ~120 concurrent model sessions.
- Max request size: ~1.5k tokens; typical < 256 tokens.
- Egress constraints: corporate firewall enforces outbound NAT; permitted IPs will be provided.
- Preferred connectivity: VPC peering (primary) with VPN fallback for DR; MTU 1500.

Immediate asks from Redwood to run a short preflight and probe:
1) We need a traceroute and single-run mtr from your inference subnets to the Redwood-maintained probe IPs (list attached).
2) Please validate that UDP/TCP keepalives are permitted across the peering path and confirm any stateful load balancers or proxies that terminate long-lived connections.
3) Share egress ACL and proxy rules (we got the XLS from Asha, thanks) — Ben will map required ports.
4) Test window: propose Tue 2027-12-07 08:00–10:00 PT for a staged streaming smoke test. Ben will coordinate an engineer-on-call.

Proposed owners and due dates:
- Sanjay / Asha: send traceroute + mtr outputs and final allowed IPs list by Fri 2027-12-03. (owner: MaplePay)
- Ben: run synthetic streaming probe, capture p50/p95/p99 and packet captures from both sides; share results within 24h of the test. (owner: Redwood)
- Karthik: produce a minimal test plan (connection handshake, MTU, TLS ciphers, websocket vs HTTP/2 fallback checks) and link to Drive doc by Mon 2027-12-06. (owner: Redwood)

Notes/assumptions:
- We'll start with a pinned model variant for deterministic performance and enable KV cache warmup during the probe.
- If peering introduces >20ms one-way jitter we’ll propose a small-capacity dedicated path for the hot traffic.

Attachments: redwood-network-probe-checklist.pdf (probe IPs + test commands), sample results format.

Thanks — looking forward to the test.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@maplepay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@maplepay.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deployment — network probe & SLO next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming we can get you the outputs you asked for. A few clarifications from our infra team below.

1) Peering: we prefer VPC peering as the primary path. Our infra team says peering will be in the same region (us-east-1) and does not NAT by default; that said our corporate egress for third-party endpoints terminates through a proxy cluster (we'll provide exact IPs).
2) Firewall/proxy: there is a stateful proxy that will rewrite headers for some long-lived TLS flows; we need to validate that websocket upgrades are preserved end-to-end. If not, we will accept HTTP/2 streaming with keep-alive.
3) MTU & fragmentation: default 1500 across our transit. We will run an MTU test as part of the traceroute output.

We can produce mtr/traceroute and the allowed-ips spreadsheet by EOD Fri (2027-12-03). Regarding the test window, Tue 2027-12-07 08:00 PT works for us; Asha will put the time on the calendar and include our network engineer.

Two asks from our side: can Redwood provide a minimal client that exercises both chunked streaming and single-response paths (sample harness) and the expected CSV format for p50/p95/p99? Also, do you have a recommended packet-capture configuration (tcpdump filters) so we capture only the relevant flows?

Sanjay
VP Platform Engineering | MaplePay
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@maplepay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment — network probe & SLO next steps

Adding a few concrete details and the small packet of instructions we'll run during the probe. I will be the tech lead for the test on Redwood's side.

What we will run from Redwood test agents:
- HTTP/2 and websocket streaming clients hitting the pinned model endpoint for ~10m steady state, then 5m burst to emulate peak.
- Synthetic traffic profile: 600 req/s sustained with bursts to 1k req/s for 5–10m. Payloads will mirror your typical median prompt (~75 tokens) and a heavy prompt (~1.2k tokens).
- Measurements we will capture: p50/p95/p99 latency per-request (end-to-end), bytes/sec, observed retransmits, TCP RTT (via packet capture), and application-level chunking latency for streaming frames.

Ben's packet-capture guidance (attach):
- tcpdump filter: host <maplepay-egress-ip> and port 443 -w capture.pcap (we'll provide exact IPs once Asha confirms).
- Capture at both sides if you can (MaplePay egress + Redwood probe). Limit to 10m capture windows to avoid disk pressure.

I attached the redwood-network-probe-checklist.pdf (probe IPs, sample tcpdump commands, expected CSV format). I will schedule a short pre-probe sync (15m) 2027-12-07 07:30 PT to walk through roles and fallbacks. Ben will be on-call during the 08:00 test.

--
Ben Carter
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@maplepay.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 05 Dec 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment — network probe & SLO next steps

Forwarding final calendar invite and checklist. Quick checklist for everyone before the pre-probe sync:
- Sanjay/Asha: confirm the final allowed-ips spreadsheet attached and send traceroute/mtr outputs to ben@redwood.inference.
- Asha: include the network engineer and the person who can open the firewall rules during the short test window.
- Karthik: drop the test plan link in the Drive doc (I added edit rights for the MaplePay group).

If we see any unexpected >30ms variance in one-way latency during the smoke run we will fail open to the HTTP/2 streaming path and capture more detail. If everything looks clean we will proceed to a 24h soak next week to confirm throughput and stability.

Thanks — see you in the pre-probe sync 12/07 07:30 PT.

--
